references.text: Laban gave his maidservant Zilpah to his daughter Leah as a maidservant – a direct parallel to how he now gives Bilhah to Rachel.
Rebekkah's nurse accompanied her when she left home to marry Isaac, a similar practice of giving a servant woman to the bride.
Rachel gave her maidservant Bilhah to Jacob as a wife so that she might have children through her, showing Bilhah's continuing role in the family.
Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, was involved in a scandalous incident with Reuben, demonstrating her continued presence in Jacob's household.
Bilhah's sons are mentioned as descendants of Rachel, and Bilhah is identified as the one Laban gave to his daughter Rachel.
Thematic parallel: Leah gives Zilpah in the same way that Rachel gave Bilhah, highlighting the repeated structure within the family.
Thematic parallel: Laban gave a female slave to Leah (Zilpah) just as he gave one to Rachel (Bilhah), illustrating his role in the family's formation.
